title: One Open Filing per Driver and Ordering State — Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing
content:
## Clause

A household may hold Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing certificates for several drivers, and one driver may need filings for more than one ordering state, so there is no cap on the number of filings per customer. A driver may have only one open filing with one ordering state. A new filing is requested only when the driver has no open filing with the same ordering state; an existing open filing is corrected, amended or reinstated instead.

## Terms used in the clause

- **Open filing:** a filing for the driver with that ordering state whose status is requested, filed, accepted, rejected or cancel-notified (an SR-26 has been sent and has not yet taken effect). A filing that is released or lapsed is not open.
- **Same driver and same ordering state:** the comparison is made on the driver the filing names together with the state that receives it. A filing for the same driver with a different ordering state, or for a different driver of the household with the same state, is a different pairing.
- **Evidence:** the household's filing records — the driver, the ordering state and the status of each filing — as the system shows them before the request is made.

## Matrix

| Existing filing for the same driver and the same ordering state | Is a new filing requested? |
|---|---|
| None | This clause does not stand in the way |
| One with status requested, filed, accepted, rejected or cancel-notified | No — the existing open filing is corrected, amended or reinstated instead |
| Only filings with status released or lapsed | This clause does not stand in the way |

## Illustrations (hypothetical household)

1. A household's two drivers each need an Ohio filing. Each driver may hold one open Ohio filing; the household holds two filings and no per-customer cap applies.
2. One driver holds an accepted Kentucky filing and receives a Tennessee order. The pairing driver–Tennessee has no open filing, so this clause does not stand in the way of a Tennessee filing.
3. One driver holds a rejected Virginia filing and asks for a Virginia filing again. The rejected filing is still open; no new filing is requested and the existing filing is the one corrected.
